title: KEPCO customer data breach, Nov 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by KEPCO, Yonhap, Chosunbiz, Financial News, Electronic Times, Aju Press, Newsis, Digital Times, Chosun Ilbo, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: KEPCO, South Korea's state-run power utility, says 1,520,248 user records were leaked across two systems; the count of distinct people is not given.
who_is_affected: Users of KEPCO ON (electricity bills and payment) and of the SRM procurement system, including company representatives and staff. KEPCO has a desk to check whether you were affected.

known.text: KEPCO says a cyber intrusion caused the leak of customers' personal data.
KEPCO detected outside illegal access attempts on Nov 20, blocked them and asked police to investigate.
KEPCO is investigating with the National Intelligence Service, the energy ministry and outside experts.
Korea's privacy regulator has opened an investigation, with an on-site inspection.
KEPCO got an email from the hacker on Nov 19 and confirmed a dark-web posting on Nov 20, the regulator says.

not_known.text: Whether this is linked to the October breach.
How many distinct people are affected, without double counting.
Whether the leaked data has been misused.
